faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Common questions about rubber component design, manufacturing, and quality assurance.

q1.question: What is the typical lead time for custom rubber parts?
q1.answer: Standard lead times range from 2-4 weeks for existing tooling, and 4-6 weeks for new tooling development. Prototype parts can often be delivered within 1-2 weeks using rapid tooling methods.

q2.question: How do I choose the right rubber material for my application?
q2.answer: Material selection depends on temperature range, chemical exposure, mechanical requirements, and application standards and operating conditions. Our material selection guide provides detailed comparison data, or contact our engineering team for recommendations.

q3.question: What tolerance levels can you achieve?
q3.answer: We routinely achieve ISO 3302 Class M1 tolerances (±0.05mm for small parts). Tighter tolerances are possible with specialized tooling and process control - consult our engineering team for feasibility.

q4.question: Do you provide PPAP documentation?
q4.answer: Yes, we provide full PPAP documentation including Level 3 submissions with all supporting data. Our quality management system is IATF 16949 certified, ensuring automotive-grade documentation standards.

q5.question: Can you work with customer-supplied materials?
q5.answer: Yes, we can process customer-supplied materials or source specific grades as required. All materials undergo incoming inspection and verification before use in production.

hero.title: The RubberQ Standard
hero.subtitle: Our two-stage mixing process — run on a single, dedicated A-mixing line designed with our Japanese formulation partners — is the backbone of our quality promise. By separating masterbatching from final compounding, we achieve superior batch-to-batch consistency across years of production for critical EV, semiconductor, and Tier 2 automotive applications.

singleLineCallout.title: Single-Line Mixing Control
singleLineCallout.body: RubberQ schedules compound families by contamination risk, runs SOP-based cleaning between batch families, and keeps A-mixing records tied to the batch. This supports high-purity and long-term repeatability needs without exposing customer-specific recipes.

hnbr.name: HNBR (Hydrogenated Nitrile)
hnbr.desc: EV thermal management hoses, high-temperature automotive seals, fuel-system O-rings. Low compression set under sustained heat and oil exposure.

fkm.name: FKM (Fluoroelastomer)
fkm.desc: Chemical, fuel, and high-temperature resistance for aerospace, semiconductor process, and high-performance automotive applications.

ffkm.name: FFKM (Perfluoroelastomer)
ffkm.desc: Our flagship co-development compound. Aggressive plasma etch, ALD/CVD chambers, high-purity gas delivery in semiconductor manufacturing.

epdm.name: EPDM (Ethylene Propylene Diene)
epdm.desc: Weather, ozone, and steam resistance. Used for EV thermal and energy-storage seals, charging infrastructure, BESS cabinets, and outdoor industrial enclosures.

nbr.name: NBR (Nitrile Rubber)
nbr.desc: Cost-effective oil resistance for hydraulic, pneumatic, pump, and general industrial sealing applications.

acm.name: ACM (Polyacrylate)
acm.desc: Automotive transmission seals. Outstanding ATF (Automatic Transmission Fluid) resistance with continuous service to 175°C.

aem.name: AEM (Ethylene Acrylate)
aem.desc: Automotive heat ducts, turbocharger hoses, and engine air management seals. Heat + oil combined resistance.

silicone.name: Silicone (HCR — Heat Cured Rubber)
silicone.desc: Industrial-grade silicone with -60°C to +230°C temperature range for electronics, clean industrial equipment, and thermal cycling applications.

lsr.name: LSR (Liquid Silicone Rubber)
lsr.desc: Precision overmolding and liquid injection for tight-tolerance components. Industrial and equipment applications where geometric precision matters.

Mixed in a shared multi-product line with cross-contamination risk
Untested by the molder before molding

rubberQItems: Designed by our Japanese formulation partners since 1995
Mixed on our dedicated single A-line (zero cross-contamination)
Tested in-house for every batch (aging, tensile, viscosity, cure)

aline.title: Our Single A-Mixing Line
aline.intro: Three operational advantages we deliberately preserve by running ONE line, not many:
aline.adv1Body: Same Banbury, same process curve, same operator team. Your 2030 PPAP file will reproduce your 2026 part exactly. Multi-line plants can't guarantee this.
aline.adv2Body: Strict cleaning SOP between batches. Sequence-ordered scheduling: highest-purity compounds first, high-carbon-black/peroxide compounds last. Critical for semiconductor FFKM and EV thermal and energy-storage seal applications.
aline.adv3Body: Every batch's rheology curve and Mooney viscosity is reviewed in real time by our lab team — not sampled. Multi-line plants only sample-check.

workflow.title: From Application to Production

stages.name: NEED ASSESSMENT
stages.desc: You describe operating conditions (temp, fluid, lifecycle). Mutual NDA in place.

stages.name: FORMULATION DESIGN
stages.desc: Japanese formulation partners propose 2-3 candidate compounds based on application chemistry.

stages.name: LAB TRIAL
stages.desc: We mix small batches (500g) and run full property tests. You receive the test report; we iterate as needed.

stages.name: PILOT MOLDING
stages.desc: Pilot tooling + small-batch molded samples for your functional validation in your end environment.

stages.name: PRODUCTION RELEASE
stages.desc: Tooling scaled to production. First-article inspection, PPAP/FAI documentation, batch traceability live.

workflow.totalNote: Total: 12-24 weeks for ground-up compound development. 4-8 weeks if optimizing an existing RubberQ compound.

abMixing.title: A-Mixing, B-Mixing, and Batch Release Control
abMixing.intro: The process flow separates masterbatch preparation from final cure-system addition. This reduces formulation drift, improves traceability, and gives the lab a defined release gate before molding.

stages.title: Masterbatch foundation
stages.body: Base polymer, filler, oil, and reinforcement materials are weighed, barcode-checked, mixed, sheeted, cooled, and screened for foreign matter before release.

stages.title: Intermediate material check
stages.body: A-compound can be checked for dispersion, specific gravity, and Mooney viscosity before it moves to final mixing.

stages.title: Cure-system addition
stages.body: Accelerators and cure-system ingredients are added later under process instruction, then the compound is matured, cut, stored, and prepared for molding.

stages.title: Lab gate before molding
stages.body: Rheometer curve, hardness, tensile strength, elongation, and drawing-specific checks confirm the batch is suitable for production.

whyChemistry.title: Why Compound Chemistry Wins in EV Applications
whyChemistry.intro: Unlike legacy ICE seals, EV seals operate in:
points: Continuous high-temperature exposure (thermal management hoses see 130-160°C constantly, not just at peak)
Compression set under long-duration static load (energy-system lifecycle = 8-15 years, not warranty replacement)
Mixed-fluid environments (coolants, dielectric fluids, electrolyte vapor)
whyChemistry.edge: Our advantage: every compound is developed with these specific service conditions in mind — not pulled off a shelf.

hero.title: FKM and FFKM Seals for Semiconductor Manufacturing
hero.subtitle: Cross-contamination tolerance in semiconductor process is near-zero. Our single dedicated A-mixing line — with sequence-ordered scheduling and validated cleaning SOP — delivers the compound purity that wafer-fab seals demand.

engagement.title: Where We Engage
engagement.intro: We engage on semiconductor sealing as a co-development service, not as an off-shelf catalog. Two engagement modes:

fkm.label: FKM-Based Process Seals (proven)
fkm.desc: Wafer handling, chamber static seals, gas-line gaskets in non-aggressive plasma environments. Built on 30 years of FKM compound development. Standard 8-16 week lead time.

ffkm.label: FFKM-Based Process Seals (co-development)
ffkm.desc: Aggressive plasma etch, ALD/CVD chamber dynamic seals, high-purity gas delivery. FFKM is our flagship co-development offering — premium chemistry, premium pricing, premium reliability. Engagement: structured 5-stage development with our Japanese formulation team, NDA-backed.

whySingleLine.title: Why Single-Line Matters in Semicon
whySingleLine.body: In a multi-line plant, yesterday's high-carbon-black batch can leave residue affecting today's FFKM batch — even with cleaning. We eliminate that risk by design: ONE A-line, sequence-ordered (high-purity first, high-filler last), validated SOP between batches. Auditable.

processCompat.title: Process Compatibility (Customer-Specified)
processCompat.body: We do not publish standard FFKM formulations — every semiconductor application has unique process chemistry (etchant gases, RF power, thermal cycling). Submit your process conditions; we'll propose compound chemistry within 2-3 weeks under NDA.
